headline: Survey of 300 banks: near-universal AI in credit, governance falling behind
body: According to a survey by FT Longitude, SAS, and Microsoft, 299 of the 300 banks polled use AI in credit and risk choices. Only 18% of banks currently maintain fully operational, embedded AI governance processes, and 42% lack defined "kill switches" to deactivate AI models that cross preset boundaries. Just 10% reported that AI makes autonomous credit or risk decisions at scale today.
note: The gap between how widely models are used and how few banks have real-time drift monitoring or a kill switch is the part risk teams can act on first.

evidence.text: According to a new survey by FT Longitude, SAS, and Microsoft, AI adoption has reached near-universal levels at financial institutions, supporting these organizations in their decision-making.
The study also found that while AI adoption continues to gain speed, governance is falling behind.

The research, which polled 300 credit, treasury and risk leaders at banks across 31 countries in June and July 2026, found that 82% of banks now use generative AI (genAI), and 41% use agentic AI in their decision-making processes. When combined with traditional, predictive AI such as machine learning (ML), 299 of the 300 banks use AI in credit and risk choices, underscoring a swift rise in adoption.
Only 18% of banks currently maintain fully operational, embedded AI governance processes, and 26% lack a dedicated AI model risk policy. A mere 19% have real-time AI model drift monitoring.
Furthermore, 42% of banks lack defined “kill switches” to deactivate AI models that cross preset boundaries, and only 36% continuously retrain or update AI models.
At present, only a few institutions permit independent AI decisions, with just 10% reporting that AI makes autonomous credit or risk decisions at scale today.
